name: Ireland
summary_text: Ireland is a calm, comfortable destination for transgender visitors. It was one of the first countries in the world to introduce legal gender recognition by self-declaration — the Gender Recognition Act 2015 lets adults change their legal gender without medical requirements — and bathroom use is unrestricted. A hate-crime law covering sexual orientation and gender identity finally took effect at the end of 2024, equality law bans discrimination in employment, housing and services, and marriage equality was approved by referendum in 2015. The caveats are stagnation and a mildly worsening climate rather than active rollback. The 2015 law is binary-only and long-promised reform (non-binary, under-16s) has stalled; transphobic hate speech remains uncriminalised after a 2024 government U-turn; a 2025 university study documented rising discrimination against sexual and gender minorities; and total hate-crime reports rose about 15% in 2025 (racism and xenophobia are the most common motives). None of this amounts to criminal exposure or physical danger for a visitor. Day-to-day, Ireland is welcoming with low violent crime and a strong civil-society support network.

sources.title: ‘For the first time, she could tell people who she was’: Ireland’s gender recognition decade | Transgender | The Guardian
sources.claim_summary: The Guardian (Dec 2025): Ireland's gender-recognition decade - reflections on the 2015 Gender Recognition Act, seen as a move away from Ireland's Catholic past; first-person accounts of what self-declaration meant.

sources.title: Irish Statute Book
sources.claim_summary: Official text of Ireland's Gender Recognition Act 2015 (electronic Irish Statute Book, updated to 2026): enables legal gender recognition by self-declaration.

sources.title: Hate Crime - Belong To - LGBTQ+ Youth Ireland
sources.claim_summary: Belong To (LGBTQ+ youth organisation): Ireland now has a hate-crime law - the Criminal Justice (Hate Offences) Act 2024 came into force in December 2024, meaning crimes motivated by LGBTQ+ identity carry enhanced punishment.

sources.title: Hate Crime Statistics 2025 - Garda
sources.claim_summary: An Garda Síochána official hate-crime statistics page (2025): police-recorded hate crime data for Ireland.

sources.title: Reports of hate crimes up 15% in 2025, with racism and xenophobia most common motives – The Irish Times
sources.claim_summary: Irish Times (Aug 2026): reports of hate crimes up 15% in 2025, with racism and xenophobia the most common motives - official Garda data reporting.

sources.title: Discrimination against sexual and gender minorities in Ireland has increased, UCD study finds – The Irish Times
sources.claim_summary: Irish Times (July 2025): a UCD study finds discrimination against sexual and gender minorities in Ireland has increased.

sources.title: 10 years on: Trans activists reflect on Gender Recognition in Ireland • GCN
sources.claim_summary: GCN (July 2025): 10 years on, trans activists reflect on the Gender Recognition Act - Ireland is one of only 11 European countries offering gender recognition through self-determination (no psychological or medical evaluation); 35 European countries still require a diagnosis, and some require sterilisation; renewed calls to address gaps in trans rights and healthcare.

sources.title: Ireland | Outright International
sources.claim_summary: Outright International country overview (updated March 2026): marriage equality by popular vote 2015; joint adoption; self-determination-based gender markers; the Equality Acts ban discrimination on 'gender' but do not explicitly cover gender identity/expression/sex characteristics (though interpreted to protect trans people under 'gender'); intersex people remain among the least protected, with nonconsensual surgeries reported in 2025.

Equaldex data for Ireland: homosexuality legal, marriage legal, gender change legal with no restrictions; gender-affirming care legal but restricted for minors; no nonbinary recognition; hate-crime protections cover SOGI; employment/housing discrimination protections cover sexual orientation only; intersex infant surgery not banned; conversion therapy not banned. High public support (61% support LGBT openness, ranked #4 of 26 regions).

sources.title: Returning and LGBTQI+ - Crosscare Irish Diaspora Support Project
sources.claim_summary: Crosscare Migrant Project guide (developed with TENI and LGBT Ireland) for LGBTQI+ Irish citizens returning to Ireland: rights, inclusive services, community reconnection - practical returnee information.

sources.title: ‘It left me traumatised’: The barriers to accessing transgender healthcare in Ireland
sources.claim_summary: The Journal Investigates (April 2025): barriers to accessing transgender healthcare in Ireland - almost 20 trans adults describe traumatic experiences and long wait times at the National Gender Service; the HSE admitted trans healthcare is 'limited' and 'not meeting people's full range of needs'.
NOTE: Not retrievable at research time (HTTP 402 paywall); the underlying Telegraph article (Sept 2024) reports Ireland backing down on hate-speech laws amid the trans debate.
